title: Overview
text: West Virginia State University (WVSU) is a public, 1890 land-grant, historically Black college/university (HBCU) in Institute, West Virginia. It is a masters-degree-granting institution described as the largest institution of higher education in the Charleston metropolitan area, and is known as a 'living laboratory of human relations'.

title: Founding and name changes
text: Founded in 1891 as the West Virginia Colored Institute and designated one of the original 1890 land-grant schools under the Second Morrill Act. Renamed West Virginia Collegiate Institute (1915), West Virginia State College (1929), and West Virginia State University (2004).

title: Motto
text: Veritas Lux Mundi (Latin), meaning 'Truth is the Light of the World'.

title: Mission
text: WVSU will meet the higher education and economic development needs of the state and region through innovative teaching and applied research.

title: Accreditation
text: Accredited by the Higher Learning Commission.

title: Land-grant status
text: One of only 19 land-grant universities designated by the Second Morrill Act in 1890 and one of only two land-grant institutions in West Virginia. Land-grant extension services aid more than 20,000 West Virginians in 38 counties. Research funding about $17 million annually (per the 2019-2021 quick facts).

title: Enrollment and student profile
text: Quick facts (older data): total enrollment Fall 2019 was 4,337; student/faculty ratio 12:1. Undergraduate profile 2020-21: 58% female, 89% in-state, 11% adult (25+), 14% minority, 63% part-time, 5% transfer, 5% international. Third-party sites in recent years report about 3,000 to 3,800 total students, so enrollment figures vary by source and year.

title: Outcomes
text: Fall-to-fall retention for full-time first-time freshmen was 60%. The 4-year graduation rate was 16% and the 6-year rate 31% (2015 cohort). 87% of alumni within six months of graduation are employed full-time, in full-time graduate school, or in the military (May 2020 cohort). 90% of students are eligible for financial assistance.

title: Campus and location
text: Located in Institute, WV 25112, about 8 miles west of Charleston, the state capital. The campus is about 123 acres with 864,287 square feet of floor space.

title: Undergraduate admissions office
text: Office of Undergraduate Recruitment & Admissions, 124 Ferrell Hall, PO Box 1000, Institute, WV 25112. Email admissions@wvstateu.edu. A copy of an unofficial transcript can be used to make an admissions decision. WVSU has rolling admissions and test scores (SAT/ACT) are optional. Third-party sites report an acceptance rate of about 96%.

title: International undergraduate admissions
text: Checklist: $20 application fee, application for admission, official transcripts, proof of English language proficiency, and a statement of purpose. Documents can be emailed to international@wvstateu.edu; phone (304) 204-4094. A third-party site lists international deadlines of about August 14 (fall) and October 1 (spring); confirm on wvstateu.edu.

title: 2026-2027 cost of attendance (undergraduate)
text: Estimated annual figures: tuition and fees $9,920 (in-state) and about $15,560 (out-of-state); books and supplies $1,330; housing and meals about $10,718 on campus, $10,850 off campus, or $6,510 living with parents; loan fees $71. Online undergraduate programs: tuition and fees $11,640 plus $1,750 online class fees. Out-of-state label is inferred from the page layout; verify on the official page.

title: 2026-2027 cost of attendance (graduate)
text: In-state graduate tuition and fees $9,990 per year; books and supplies $1,330; housing and meals $9,760 on campus or $10,850 off campus; loan fees $155; transportation $1,380. Online graduate: tuition and fees $9,990 plus $1,500 online class fees, estimated total $12,975.

title: Fee schedule and meal plans
text: WVSU publishes a Schedule of Fees per semester (FY26 version: wvstateu.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/03/FY26-Fee-Schedule.pdf). Earlier schedules list a commuter meal plan of about $400 per semester and board plans around $2,500 to $2,900 per semester. Students living in campus housing must have a meal plan.

title: Residence hall rates 2026-2027
text: Per semester: Dawson Hall double $2,479, single $3,621. Sullivan Hall double $1,750, single $2,000. Keith Hall 2-, 3- or 4-bedroom suite $3,881 each. Duplex A and B (Marshall aviation students) $3,950. Non-refundable room reservation fee $200. Rates for 2025-2026 were the same except Sullivan Hall double $1,500 and single $1,750.

title: Housing office
text: Office of Housing and Residence Life: phone 304.766.5057, email reslife@wvstateu.edu. Priority housing deadline for 2025-26 was July 1, and housing does not guarantee specific room types or halls. Students must submit the housing application, pay the reservation fee, and be enrolled for the term.

title: Colleges
text: WVSU is reorganizing its academic colleges from four to three, so some web pages are in transition. One of the three is the College of Business, Sciences, and Technology. The College of Professional Studies covers areas such as Education, Health and Human Performance, Nursing, Social Work and Criminal Justice.

title: Programs and degrees
text: Quick facts (2019-20): 72 academic programs, including 23 baccalaureate programs, 7 master's programs and 7 fully online programs. Examples include Biology, Chemistry, Computer Science, Mathematics, Engineering (Civil and Chemical emphasis), Business and Economics (concentrations such as Accounting, Finance, Marketing, Management and Management Information Systems), English, Music (BA), Health Science, Sport Studies, Education and Interdisciplinary Studies. Graduate: Biotechnology, Computer Science, Media Studies, Master of Education in Instructional Leadership, and EdD in Leadership Studies.

title: Drain-Jordan Library overview
text: The Drain-Jordan Library holds nearly 150,000 book volumes plus e-books, e-journals, government documents, and non-print and archival resources. Website: library.wvstateu.edu and wvstateu.edu/students/current-students/library. Address: Drain-Jordan Library, WVSU, PO Box 1002, Campus Box L17, Institute, WV 25112-1002. Main phone (304) 766-3116; reference desk (304) 766-3135.

title: Services and help
text: Ask-A-Librarian by chat or email (email answered within 48 hours Monday to Friday during semesters; chat only during library hours), reference desk email refdesk@wvstateu.edu, and in-person help during library hours. Laptops can be borrowed for 3-hour periods. Daily Charleston Gazette newspapers are in the Periodicals section; the student newspaper is online at YJOnline. Interlibrary loan (ILL) is available. Distance learners can return materials by book drop or mail.

title: Databases and LibGuides
text: The library offers research databases (including EBSCOhost) listed at library.wvstateu.edu/DB-sets/DB-index.html; not all databases work off campus. Subject guides are at wvstateu.libguides.com (for example Nursing Resources, Government Documents, and an Introduction to Library Resources). Older pathfinders cover subjects like Biology and Criminal Justice.

title: Archives and Special Collections
text: Located on the ground floor (Room 2) of the Drain-Jordan Library, by appointment during library hours. Holdings cover university history, African Americans in West Virginia, African-American higher education, West Virginia and Appalachian history, including rare books, photographs, manuscripts, recordings and maps. Contact refdesk@wvstateu.edu or 304-766-3135.

title: Federal depository
text: The Drain-Jordan Library has been a member of the Federal Depository Library Program (FDLP) since 1907, providing free public access to government information.

title: Teams and affiliation
text: NCAA Division II, Mountain East Conference. Men's sports: baseball, basketball, football, golf, tennis. Women's sports: basketball, softball, tennis, volleyball, soccer. Spirit groups: cheerleading and dance team. Colors: Old Gold and Black.

title: Mascot
text: The mascot is a Yellow Jacket named Stinger. Fans call themselves the Yellow Jacket Nation.

title: Cybersecurity Innovation Center (CIC)
text: The Cybersecurity Innovation Center at West Virginia State University advances cybersecurity education, applied research, and real-world innovation through hands-on labs, collaborative projects, and student-centered learning. Its work emphasizes critical-infrastructure protection, including agriculture and other essential sectors, and connects education, workforce development, research, community engagement, and industry.

title: Dr. Ali Al-Sinayyid profile
text: Dr. Ali Al-Sinayyid is an Assistant Professor of Computer Science and Director of the Cybersecurity Innovation Center (CIC) at WVSU. He holds a Ph.D. in Computer Science from Southern Illinois University Carbondale and has more than 17 years of combined academic and industry experience. His work includes critical-infrastructure cybersecurity, operational technology and industrial control systems (OT/ICS/SCADA), CyberAI, Internet of Things security, cybersecurity education, workforce development, and applied research.

title: Cybersecurity degree and Google Cybersecurity Clinic
text: WVSU's four-year Bachelor of Science in Cybersecurity was approved in 2025 and offers General Cybersecurity and Agricultural Cybersecurity options. WVSU's faculty profile identifies it as the only university in West Virginia offering the Agricultural Cybersecurity option. Dr. Ali Al-Sinayyid led development of the degree and directs the WVSU Google Cybersecurity Clinic. His profile lists a $1 million Google.org-supported clinic grant; the clinic opened in March 2025 as the first cybersecurity clinic of its type in West Virginia and provides no-cost cybersecurity support while giving students applied experience.

title: CIC hands-on cybersecurity labs
text: The CIC describes several hands-on labs: CyberHive uses physical SCADA, PLC, and HMI environments to train students to monitor, attack, and defend industrial systems such as chemical and water treatment plants. KITE is a portable modular industrial-control training platform built with real components. The Robotics and Autonomous Systems lab covers AI/ML, computer vision, and autonomous robotics. CyberCity is a smart-city cyber-physical testbed spanning agriculture, transportation, energy, water, and IoT-enabled buildings. HoneyNet is a controlled honeypot environment for studying real-world attack behavior and threat intelligence.

title: CIC research and publication topics
text: CIC research connects cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, computer science, IoT, cloud computing, operational technology, industrial control systems, and critical infrastructure. Research topics highlighted by the center include machine-learning methods for IoT attack detection, DDoS defense in cloud computing, time-based blind SQL injection detection, blockchain security for SCADA/ICS, phishing detection, intrusion detection for advanced persistent threats, and code-injection defense. Publication totals can differ between WVSU page snapshots, so consult the current CIC page for its latest list rather than relying on a fixed count.

title: Selected cybersecurity grants led by Dr. Ali Al-Sinayyid
text: The WVSU faculty profile lists selected projects including a $1,000,000 Google Cybersecurity Clinics Fund award (Principal Investigator, 2024-2030); a $749,973 U.S. Department of Energy and Marshall University critical-infrastructure center grant (Co-Principal Investigator, 2022-2026); a $500,000 Marshall University partnership for CIC expansion (Co-Principal Investigator, 2023-2026); a $764,792 Kanawha County Commission grant supporting the CIC (Co-Principal Investigator, 2022); and a $349,681 CISE-MSI research award (Co-Principal Investigator, 2023-2025). These are selected profile-listed awards, not a complete or independently audited funding total.
